thread:
Sam: @Priya shared a customer report — their invoice endpoint intermittently returns 0 for `amount` even when the payload contained a numeric string. They hit this in production, billing impacted.
Priya: Repro steps attached from the customer: they POST with `amount` = \"\" (empty string) for some items and expect a validation error, but our structured mode returns `0`.
Sam: Paste of their request:
```json
{
  \"invoice_id\": \"inv_123\",
  \"items\": [{\"id\": \"sku_1\", \"amount\": \"\"}]
}
```
Sam: Expected: parse error or explicit null/quoted string preserved per schema. Actual: response body contains `\"amount\": 0`.
Priya: Customer says toggling to non-structured (free-form) avoided the issue but they need structured for downstream validation.
Eve: Can you paste the response they got?
Priya: Response snippet from model stream (customer captured):
```json
{\n  \"invoice_id\": \"inv_123\",\n  \"items\": [{\"id\": \"sku_1\", \"amount\": 0}]\n}
```
Priya: They also attached the raw stream capture — the token boundary cut happened right after the colon.
Sam: @Jordan can you check if there were any stream truncations or proxy timeouts around their request_ts: 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z?
Jordan: Looking at gateway logs — no 5xx, but I see a couple of TCP retransmits to the host that handled the stream at 14:12:03. Trace ID x-rt-9987 shows chunked transfer with a 2s gap between chunks.
Jordan: The runtime's parser has this path: when streaming and using structured/strict JSON mode, if a numeric field token is cut mid-stream and the next chunk resumes with an empty token (e.g., `""`), the fallback coercion pipeline attempts numeric coercion and returns 0. That's a bug.
InfraBot: @Eve assigned to eng-runtime for triage (ticket INF-4421).
Eve: Thanks. Quick repro I ran locally replicates the behavior:
curl command:
```bash
curl -s -N -X POST \ 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \ 
  -d '\{"invoice_id":"inv_123","items":[{"id":"sku_1","amount":""}]\}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?structured_output=true&strict_json=true
```
Eve: With a simulated chunk boundary (sleep between chunks) the model response becomes `amount: 0` in the final JSON. Without chunk boundary it returns an explicit empty string token (or throws validation).
Sam: Is the coercion happening in the runtime or in the post-processing conversion step?
Eve: It's in the structured output post-processor that attempts to coerce scalar tokens into the requested schema types. When a partial token is observed, we treat it as empty and fall back to numeric default 0.
Eve: Root cause: streaming chunk boundary + strict structured mode + empty-string token path -> numeric defaulting.
Priya: Customer impact: invoices charged incorrectly for a small subset of requests that happened to hit chunk boundaries. They saw ~0.3% of requests affected.
Sam: Proposed mitigations: 1) short-term: set `strict_json=false` or disable streaming for their route; 2) mid-term: runtime fix to not coerce empty-string to numeric default, instead surface parse error; 3) postmortem + notify billing.
Jordan: I'll add a runtime rule to retry a single chunk fetch when we detect a partial token (cheap). Will monitor for regressions.
Eve: I'll open PR to change coercion behavior so empty string doesn't map to 0 and to add unit tests covering chunked token boundaries. Ticket linked INF-4421.
Sam: Sam to PM for customer comms: recommend turning off streaming for their Dedicated pool until patch rolled out.
Priya: Customer accepted the workaround and requested ETA. Can we give them a window?
Eve: ETA for a patch to dev->canary in 48 hours, prod rollout in 7 days assuming canary looks good.
Sam: Noted. I'll update the support ticket and flag billing ops. :thumbsup:
